claim: Henderson et al. name a taxonomy of specific, individually decisive, often-unreported implementation/reporting factors in deep RL: network architecture/activation, reward scale, random seeds and trial count, environment dynamics, and codebase/reimplementation differences.
stance_target: N1: prior work already names a taxonomy of unreported implementation confounds that are each individually decisive for a headline
scope_conditions: Continuous-control deep policy-gradient RL (TRPO, DDPG, PPO, ACKTR), OpenAI Gym MuJoCo tasks
quoted_support: Reproducibility can be affected by extrinsic factors (e.g. hyperparameters or codebases) and intrinsic factors (e.g. effects of random seeds or environment properties). We investigate these sources of variance in reported results through a representative set of experiments.

claim: Henderson et al. explicitly attribute dramatic performance differences to implementation details not reflected in publications, using different codebases (OpenAI baselines TRPO, original Schulman 2015 TRPO, rllab TensorFlow TRPO) as the controlled manipulation.
stance_target: N1 sub-claim (a): naming unreported implementation choices as individually decisive
scope_conditions: TRPO and DDPG across three independent codebase implementations
quoted_support: We find that implementation differences which are often not reflected in publications can have dramatic impacts on performance.

claim: Henderson et al. show that which algorithm is reported as 'best' reverses depending on the environment: DDPG outperforms all methods in stable-dynamics environments (e.g. HalfCheetah-v1), while TRPO significantly outperforms elsewhere.
stance_target: N1 sub-claim (c): prior work shows a published ranking changes under a controlled protocol
scope_conditions: OpenAI Gym MuJoCo continuous control: Hopper, HalfCheetah, Swimmer, Walker
quoted_support: in environments with stable dynamics (e.g. HalfCheetah-v1), DDPG outperforms all... TRPO significantly outperforms

claim: Henderson et al. never fit an ANOVA or report an eta^2-style variance-decomposition attribution of how much of a headline metric each confound explains individually and jointly, nor do they show confounds netting UP when combined.
stance_target: N1: the quantitative eta^2 decomposition and confound-interaction-nets-up finding are already owned by prior reality-check work
quoted_support: we explore several significance measures which give insight ... Generally, we find that the significance values match

claim: Henderson et al.'s confound taxonomy is entirely policy-gradient-RL-specific (reward scaling, MuJoCo stochastic dynamics, codebase reimplementation drift) with no analogue to offline MBO's surrogate-model confounds (target scaling, candidate/oracle protocol, ensemble size K, acquisition pessimism beta).
stance_target: residual specific to offline MBO not owned by this paper
scope_conditions: cross-domain comparison, deep RL vs offline MBO
quoted_support: Due to the significant effects of hyperparameters (particularly reward scaling), another possibly important line of [investigation]

claim: Henderson et al. manipulate confounds one at a time within a family of RL algorithms rather than running a crossed factorial across two orthogonal design axes (e.g. surrogate model class x optimizer/search class).
stance_target: N6: the crossed surrogate x optimizer factorial design is already owned by prior reality-check work
scope_conditions: Experimental design structure of the paper
quoted_support: For clarity, we focus our investigation on policy gradient (PG) methods in continuous control.

claim: Henderson et al. claim to be the first work to address reproducibility and good experimental practice as a central question in deep RL specifically.
stance_target: field-of-origin claim, relevant to dating the reality-check genre
scope_conditions: Deep reinforcement learning literature as of 2017-2018
quoted_support: to the best of our knowledge this is the first work to address this important question in the context of deep RL.
